answer: A livestock-registry anchor ties each agent to real animals: the agent must present an ear-tag record from the national livestock registry, countersigned by a vet, for umber-coated cattle grazing on the delta pasture, with the herd's home farm as the vertex of three vet visits. The registry allows one active agent per herd, so a Sybil clone reusing the same tags is rejected as a duplicate, and a fake herd has no vet signature at all.
